files.docs/dialect.md:
# The `crmcsv` dialect

This is NOT RFC 4180 and the Python `csv` module cannot parse it. Implement it exactly.

The text is UTF-8. If it begins with a BOM (U+FEFF) the BOM is not data.

## Records

* A record ends at `\r\n` or at `\n`. A lone `\r` outside a quoted field is ordinary data.
* At the start of a record, a physical line whose first character is `#` is a COMMENT: the whole
  physical line is discarded. A `#` anywhere else, including on a continuation line inside a
  quoted field, is ordinary data.
* At the start of a record, a completely empty physical line is discarded.
* The first surviving record is the header.

## Fields

Fields are separated by `,`.

A field that begins with `"` is QUOTED. Scan forward from after that quote:

* `""` produces one `"` and scanning continues.
* A backslash consumes the character after it: `\n` produces a newline, `\t` a tab, `\r` a
  carriage return, and any other `\x` produces `x` (so `\"` is a quote and `\\` is a backslash).
  A backslash escape is applied before the quote rules, so the `"` in `\"` never closes a field
  and the second backslash of `\\` never escapes anything.
* A raw newline is ordinary data.
* Any other `"` closes the quoted part.

After the closing quote, scanning CONTINUES in the unquoted rules below and whatever it produces
is appended to the same field, so `"quoted"tail` is the single field `quotedtail`.

An UNQUOTED field, or the continuation after a closing quote, runs until a `,`, a `\n`, or a `\r`
that is immediately followed by `\n` - whichever comes first - and the same backslash escapes
apply, so `a\,b` is the single field `a,b`.

## NULL

A field is NULL if and only if it was never quoted and its raw text, before any unescaping, is
exactly the two characters `\N`. Everything else is a string, so the quoted field `"\N"` is the
one-character string `N` and the unquoted field `x\N` is the string `xN`.

## Writing it back out

`dump(rows)` renders records separated by `\n`, with a trailing `\n`, and each record is one
physical line. Each field:

1. NULL is written as the two characters `\N` and nothing else.
2. Otherwise take the value and replace `\` with `\\`, then newline with `\n`, carriage return
   with `\r`, and tab with `\t` (two characters each).
3. The field is then QUOTED - wrapped in `"` with every `"` in the result doubled to `""` - if
   and only if the original value is the empty string, or contains `,` or `"`, or the field is
   the first field of its record and the original value starts with `#`. Otherwise it is written
   bare.

`parse(dump(rows)) == rows` must hold for every row list, including NULLs, empty strings,
backslashes, quotes, newlines and tabs.

files.tests/test_dialect.py:
"""Pinned behaviour of etl.dialect. Part of the specification; must pass unmodified."""
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from etl.dialect import parse, dump   # noqa: E402

rows = parse('a,b\n1,"x,y"\n')
assert rows == [["a", "b"], ["1", "x,y"]], rows

assert parse('q,"He said ""hi"" and \\"bye\\""\n') == [["q", 'He said "hi" and "bye"']]
assert parse('q,"ends \\\\",z\n') == [["q", "ends \\", "z"]]
assert parse('q,"quoted"tail\n') == [["q", "quotedtail"]]
assert parse("q,a\\,b\n") == [["q", "a,b"]]

assert parse("k,\\N\n") == [["k", None]]
assert parse('k,"\\N"\n') == [["k", "N"]]
assert parse("k,x\\N\n") == [["k", "xN"]]

assert parse("# skip me\nk,v\n#skip\n") == [["k", "v"]]
assert parse('k,"line\n#not a comment"\n') == [["k", "line\n#not a comment"]]
assert parse("k,v\n\n\nk2,v2\n") == [["k", "v"], ["k2", "v2"]]
assert parse("\ufeffk,v\r\nk2,v2\r\n") == [["k", "v"], ["k2", "v2"]]

nasty = [
    ["#lead", "plain", None],
    ["", "a,b", 'has "quotes"'],
    ["back\\slash", "tab\there", "nl\nhere"],
    ["\\N", "N", "cr\rhere"],
]
text = dump(nasty)
assert len(text.rstrip("\n").split("\n")) == len(nasty), "one physical line per record"
assert parse(text) == nasty, (parse(text), nasty)
assert parse(dump(parse(text))) == nasty

print("OK test_dialect")
